messages:
sam: Quick heads-up — while onboarding mariner-32k int4 I hit an intermittent "split->append->resume" cache inconsistency. Prefill ~=11.8k tokens, append ~=8k, resume generation. Intermittent duplication (3-7 toks) at the join and the KV fingerprint changes after append. Repro rate ~1/250 on perf nodes.

ivy: Which deployment? Dedicated QA or perf-lab? Any short logs?

sam: Dedicated QA pool (ded-onboard-5). Minimal failing snippet below.

```
[cache] prefill slot=12 id=0x9f1a fp=0x7c8a len=11888 epoch=94
[cache] append slot=12 id=0x9f1b fp=0x7c8b len+=8192 epoch=94
gen: step=11892 token=409 dup_span=11890-11894
[cache] fingerprint_mismatch expected=0x7c8a got=0x7c8b
```

chen: If kv_policy=reset fixes it that's a pointer to fold/merge semantics. Did you try it?

sam: Yes — reset is a deterministic workaround but adds ~20ms P50 which breaks our low-latency SLO. We need kv_policy=fold to be safe and fast.

ortega: Two likely classes: RoPE phase continuity (posclamp/posscale re-eval) at stitch time OR a metadata ordering/race where append writes metadata without a proper barrier and the generator reads a mixed view. Which arch did you hit?

sam: Seen on x86 and arm64; freq appears slightly higher on arm64.

ivy: Can you dump per-layer phase checksums after the stitch? If a specific layer flips that's a posscale/phase bug. If checksums are identical but fingerprint differs, that points to metadata race.

sam: Uploaded artifacts: /artifacts/mariner32k/snap-1798500000.tar.gz (includes token snips, slot dumps, stitch logs). Added quick repro: /tmp/mariner_split_repro.sh.

ci-bot: Created issue #5312: "mariner-32k: intermittent split-append fingerprint drift under fold" (reporter: sam) :bug:

chen: Plan proposal: 1) Add lightweight per-layer phase checksum in stitcher and run 50k deterministic iterations under qemu-int4 (seeded RNG) across both archs. 2) Instrument an atomic CAS+membar around fingerprint update as a toggle — if CAS removes repro, it's ordering. 3) Add a pos_continuity toggle that forces appended segment to use strict offset continuation; if that eliminates dup, it's RoPE continuity.

ortega: Also add a short scoped mutex on append->merge only for the experiment, not as a permanent fix. If mutex removes repro we know it's a race and can design a low-overhead handshake (epoch-token validate + CAS) later.

ivy: I'll add the phase-check hook and a tiny unit test that simulates prefill+append+resume with quantized kernels under qemu. Run both toggles (CAS-on/CAS-off, pos_continuity on/off) across 100k iterations in perf-lab.

sam: Sounds good. If CAS helps but pos_continuity also helps then we may have two independent failure modes: a rare ordering race + a posscale edge-case. We'll need both a handshake and a posscale sanity-check on stitch.

chen: Note: there was a prior async merge path in the append handler that didn't publish an epoch barrier on some paths — I flagged it in a PR a while back. I'll re-open that diff and add a targeted membar/CAS there for the experiment.

ortega: Also ensure the unit runs execute on both arm64 perf nodes and x86 qemu. Weak memory ordering on arm64 can amplify races that x86 hides.

ci-bot: CI patchset 8102 created for branch "onboard/mariner32k/split-diagnostics" and assigned to @ivy.

sam: TL;DR: intermittent duplication at prefill->append join for mariner-32k int4 under kv_policy=fold; reset is a reliable but slow workaround. Running phased experiments: phase checksums, CAS membar, scoped mutex, pos_continuity. Will post 100k run results + failing slot diffs. :mag:
